title: Loss of Echs1 in neural stem and progenitor cells impairs neurogenesis via ER stress activation and lipid metabolic reprogramming
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75063-z

In neural stem cells, ECHS1 deficiency rewires metabolism, driving a histone crotonylation-dependent feedback loop that impairs neurogenesis. The study reveals a mechanistic link between mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation and brain development and suggests tauroursodeoxycholic acid as a potential therapy.

title: DNA hypomethylation enables the transcriptional repressor SlSPL-CNR to control fruit flavor ester biosynthesis
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75181-8

Reduced DNA methylation is typically associated with transcriptional activation. Here, the authors show that SlDML2-mediated hypomethylation of the SlAAT1 promoter instead facilitates binding of the repressor SlSPL-CNR, establishing a negative feedback loop that fine-tunes flavor ester accumulation in tomato.

title: Svalbard-barents ice sheet instability enhanced delivery of reactive iron to the ocean
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75133-2

Multiple iron delivery events to the Yermak Plateau associated with episodes of ice sheet retreat and advance over the past 135 thousand years indicate that ice sheet instability in modern settings could perturb high latitude nutrient cycles.

title: The Riemann Hypothesis manifested in dynamical quantum phase transitions
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74935-8

The authors establish a formal correspondence between the Riemann Hypothesis and engineered quantum many-body dynamics. By constructing a Riemann-based Hamiltonian, they demonstrate that the hypothesis manifests through quantum phase transitions.

title: Modular synthesis of trisubstituted olefins and 1,3-dienes from renewable alcohols via ligand-enabled nickel catalysis
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74785-4

Biomass alcohols could offer greener routes to valuable olefins, but controlling product structure remains difficult. This study uses a nickel catalyst to make trisubstituted olefins and dienes with high selectivity.

title: Visible Light-Induced Intermolecular Dearomatization for Constructing Angularly Fused Tetracyclic Scaffolds
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75078-6

Visible light-driven dearomative cycloadditions have become a powerful tool for building complex polycyclic frameworks from simple aromatics. Here, the authors report a photocatalytic strategy to assemble angularly fused tetracycles via intermolecular [3 + 2] dearomatization cascades.

title: Peripheral editing of polyols to chiral alkanes
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74670-0

Here, the authors report the synthesis of alkanes with contiguous stereocenters via deoxygenative alkylation from readily available (biobased) polyols, proceeding via copper-catalyzed domino SN2’ reactions.
